newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares retreat after sharp rally.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares retreat after sharp rally.

text.p: Shares across Indian bourses ended lower on Thursday in slow, cautious trade as players booked profits and moved to the sidelines, brokers said.
They said the market lacked follow-up support after prices soared on Wednesday.
The benchmark Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index fell 35.32 points, or 1.08 percent, to 3,225.24 -- after vaulting 175.36 points, or 5.68 percent, on Wednesday.
"I wouldn't be comfortable at creating long positions at these levels," said Maulik Sharedalal at brokerage Maulik Girish. "I would rather wait for a correction."
Analysts said Wednesday's rally was triggered by expectations and some positive statements by the Indian government, but other economic news was disheartening.

"Export figures are down, inflation is rising," said Sharedalal. "This market cannot sustain a rally on statements alone." Traders said some domestic funds were sellers at higher levels, both on Wednesday and Thursday.
They said foreign funds were mostly inactive but watchful.
"A minor trigger can bring this market down," said one dealer at a foreign broking firm. "The rally was solely driven by speculative purchases."
The Delhi share index fell 7.40 points to 704.85.

The index had jumped 3.3 percent on Wednesday after Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda said on Tuesday that government planned by mid-January to announce moves to boost industrial production and revive capital markets.

At the BSE, Bajaj Auto dropped 26.25 rupees to 894, ACC 45.25 to 1,275, BSES 12.0 to 215.75, SBI 6.0 to 240.50, TELCO 5.50 to 356.50, Indian Hotel 13.75 to 718, Hindustan Lever 7.0 to 810, Reliance 4.75 to 213.25 and TISCO 2.75 to 179.50.
Ranbaxy firmed 10.0 to 592.50, Hindalco 5.0 to 673.75, Grasim 3.75 to 425 and SAIL 1.0 to 22.25.
